title: Turn off screen when PM-inhibiting app is not the active app
line: When the app keeping the screen on has all its windows minimized, the screen now dims and turns off as usual while the computer still stays awake.
explanation: PowerDevil treated every "keep the screen on" inhibition the same, no matter whether anyone could see the app that asked for it, so an app playing in a minimized window kept the screen on until it quit. PowerDevil only gets the inhibiting app's name and has no idea of its windows. The policy agent now watches the window list (libtaskmanager) while screen inhibitions exist and matches each inhibition's app name to the windows' app id or name. If the app has windows and all of them are minimized, its inhibition only blocks sleep, so dimming and screen-off run normally; inhibitions with no matching window (file transfers, background services) still keep the screen on.

commits.message:
daemon: let the screen turn off when the inhibiting app is minimized

An app that keeps the screen on, like a video player, kept it on even
when all its windows were minimized and nobody could see them. Its screen
inhibition now only keeps the system awake while that is the case.

BUG: 378404

media.caption: Master: Dolphin holds a "Playing video" screen inhibition and is minimized; after 50 s idle (turn off after 40 s) the screen is still on.
With the fix, same steps: the screen turns off at 40 s (DPMS off) while sleep stays blocked.
